fields.description: ZEN is explicitly named in Neuromeka’s V20251205 catalog as a wheeled humanoid with foldable height 1.46–1.86 m. Its 21 body DOF exclude dexterous hands and comprise 19 joints plus two drive wheels. Each four-finger hand has 13 active DOF. The table specifies 5 kg horizontal load per arm including hand and 96.5 cm maximum arm including-hand length, which is not substituted for conventional reach. It lists 0.6 m/s maximum chassis speed, 40 Ah battery capacity, eight-hour operation and six-hour charging without complete test conditions. Arm repeat positioning accuracy 0.5 mm and chassis point-to-point repeatability 1.5 cm are distinct measures. A September 2025 unveiling is documented, but current delivery, independent performance and first-sale date remain unverified.

Battery capacity is printed 40 Ah, operating duration 8 h and charging time 6 h. No battery voltage is supplied here, so Ah is not converted into Wh; load and charging test conditions remain unspecified.
The table lists five RGB cameras, 2280 dual-hand ITPU tactile processing units and 6840 tactile channels. These are manufacturer architecture counts, not independent sensing validation.
The history names ZEN among humanoids unveiled in September 2025. This establishes an unveiling milestone, not verified first commercial sale, current stock or complete portfolio coverage.

fields.description: EIR is Neuromeka’s upper-body-centered dual-arm humanoid platform. The company-hosted December 29, 2025 article, credited to Pinpointnews, explicitly describes 18 independently actuated upper-body axes: seven per arm and four across neck and waist. Its lower body is a cart-based mobile structure, which does not by itself prove autonomous AMR travel or bipedal walking. VisionX text-prompt manipulation and MimicX imitation learning are manufacturer software positioning. The stated 100 µm-level control precision is not treated as measured repeatability. The article planned a CES 2026 debut and phased production from March 2026; the old plan is not proof that production, delivery or final specifications occurred. An unnamed surgical column in the catalog is not assigned to EIR.

highlights: The exact Moby-Agri 650 Type dimension/mass row is 1400 × 855 × 491 mm and 255 kg. The other type remains a separate configuration; no extra generic platform row is counted.
A second Dimension row prints 1400 × 1900 × 450 mm without clear assembly scope. It is retained as an unresolved dimension ambiguity, not silently used to overwrite the explicitly typed body row.

Shared Moby-Agri specification: differential drive, 2D LiDAR/SLAM, maximum ground speed 1 m/s and maximum rail speed 0.4 m/s. Rail mounting/dismounting is greenhouse-specific, not an all-terrain outdoor rating.
Caster payload is explicitly 150 kg per unit. No complete-platform transport payload is established by multiplying or transferring this component rating.

The imaging module has two DOF: rotation and lift. Camera-lift bounds are printed minimum 2000 mm and maximum 4100 mm, tolerance ±5 mm and lift speed 200 mm/s; these are not body height, cargo lift ratings, docking accuracy or ground travel speed.
Lithium-ion battery is 48 VDC and 9250 Wh; maximum driving duration is 10 h with mode/load conditions unspecified. Charging duration is not established.

The current page describes crop observation including heights above 3 m and greenhouse coverage up to 10,000 m². These are application claims, not guaranteed hourly area rate, crop yield improvement or independent navigation tests.

The catalog chapter is marked KOREA ONLY. Shared family values are attributed to Moby-Agri types only where the specification table groups them; exact current regional availability remains unverified.

after.description: ZEN is explicitly named in Neuromeka’s V20251205 catalog as a wheeled humanoid with foldable height 1.46–1.86 m. Its 21 body DOF exclude dexterous hands and comprise 19 joints plus two drive wheels. Each four-finger hand has 13 active DOF. The table specifies 5 kg horizontal load per arm including hand and 96.5 cm maximum arm including-hand length, which is not substituted for conventional reach. It lists 0.6 m/s maximum chassis speed, 40 Ah battery capacity, eight-hour operation and six-hour charging without complete test conditions. Arm repeat positioning accuracy 0.5 mm and chassis point-to-point repeatability 1.5 cm are distinct measures. A September 2025 unveiling is documented, but current delivery, independent performance and first-sale date remain unverified.

after.description: NAMI is the exact name shown on Neuromeka’s current humanoid platform page. The page positions the lineup around VLA, field-data collection, teleoperation and imitation learning, but its numerical specification is carried in image content not visually inspected here. Manufacturer history and the older catalog separately use NAMY; a current table image has NAMY.png alt metadata. These clues do not establish a rename, equivalence or distinct hardware. NAMI is retained as the current named identity while NAMY remains an unresolved historical-name lead. No unnamed service/factory/surgical table is assigned to NAMI.

after.dof: 18 independently actuated upper-body axes: 7 per arm + 4 across neck and waist
after.description: EIR is Neuromeka’s upper-body-centered dual-arm humanoid platform. The company-hosted December 29, 2025 article, credited to Pinpointnews, explicitly describes 18 independently actuated upper-body axes: seven per arm and four across neck and waist. Its lower body is a cart-based mobile structure, which does not by itself prove autonomous AMR travel or bipedal walking. VisionX text-prompt manipulation and MimicX imitation learning are manufacturer software positioning. The stated 100 µm-level control precision is not treated as measured repeatability. The article planned a CES 2026 debut and phased production from March 2026; the old plan is not proof that production, delivery or final specifications occurred. An unnamed surgical column in the catalog is not assigned to EIR.

RAXIS is explicitly named in Neuromeka’s manufacturer chronology among humanoid platforms unveiled in September 2025, also reproduced in the V20251205 catalog history. This establishes a historical named platform lead. The current humanoid page’s extracted text names NAMI and EIR; it does not establish RAXIS retirement or equivalence to another platform. Exact RAXIS technical specifications and present availability remain unverified, and no unnamed service/factory/surgical numerical column is assigned to it.

companyFocuses.name: Neuromeka
companyFocuses.role: Developer of collaborative/industrial robots and robot-automation components,software and integration solutions
highlights: Neuromeka’s named arm portfolio includes original Indy models, distinct V3/IndyEye Pro/research variants, welding-oriented OPTi, NURI C/S/high-payload arms and D-series delta robots. Model generations and application equipment remain separate identities.

The manufacturer also publishes mobile and humanoid platforms, controllers, actuators, vision, teaching software and remote/service offerings. Components, software and bundled application cells do not automatically count as additional whole robot models.

Direct teaching, impedance control, sensorless collision detection, integrated vision and joint torque sensing are manufacturer features with model/family scope. Safety, certification, local-content, ROI and exclusivity claims are not independently certified here.

The download page labels the English catalogV20260903, but the linked file cover and metadata identifyV20251205. That December2025 source edition and its TBD values remain explicit rather than being presented as a newly authored September2026 catalog.

The named mobile portfolio includes versioned Moby-RP V3.3 and two Moby-Agri dimensional configurations. Platform payload, per-wheel/per-caster capacity, arm load and camera motion retain separate scopes. Catalog mobile chapters are marked KOREA ONLY.

Humanoid text explicitly names ZEN, current NAMI, EIR and historical RAXIS. Historical NAMY versus current NAMI remains an unresolved name relationship without a second counted physical model. Unnamed service/factory/surgical table columns remain unmapped.

EIR’s company-hosted December 29, 2025 article describes an 18-axis upper body and mobile cart. Its March 2026 phased-production plan is not proof of actual production, delivery or bipedal/autonomous travel.
